summary: The bad() entry point contains embedded malicious code: it decodes a hardcoded Base64 string ("Y2FsYy5leGU=" = "calc.exe") and passes it to Runtime.getRuntime().exec(), executing an attacker-chosen command with no legitimate purpose or input. The fix removes the embedded payload decode-and-execute logic. There is no legitimate feature to preserve here (the command string is a hardcoded embedded payload, not a user-driven feature), so the entry point is reduced to a benign no-op matching the good() behavior, eliminating the source-to-sink flow while leaving the class structure, entry point, and test harness intact.
